content.subject: Network Theory
content.hook: Why does a sharper resonance curve actually mean a narrower bandwidth?
content.question: A series RLC circuit has a resonant frequency of 1000 radians per second and a quality factor of 10. What is its bandwidth?
content.answerLine: The bandwidth of the circuit is 100 radians per second.
explanation: Resonance in a series RLC network happens when inductive reactance equals capacitive reactance completely.
At this resonant condition, the net reactive part vanishes and circuit impedance is purely resistive.
Quality factor measures how selective the circuit is, defined as resonant frequency divided by bandwidth.
Bandwidth represents the frequency spread between two half power points where power drops to half.
content.funFact: Radio receivers use high quality factor series resonance to isolate one clean broadcast frequency.
content.outro: Remember that quality factor inversely scales bandwidth. Follow for more state engineering exam practice!

script.narration: Resonance in a series RLC network happens when inductive reactance equals capacitive reactance completely.
At this resonant condition, the net reactive part vanishes and circuit impedance is purely resistive.
Quality factor measures how selective the circuit is, defined as resonant frequency divided by bandwidth.
Bandwidth represents the frequency spread between two half power points where power drops to half.
Rearranging the definition gives bandwidth equal to resonant frequency divided by the circuit quality factor.
Substitute 1000 radians per second for resonant frequency and 10 for the dimensionless quality factor.
Dividing 1000 by 10 yields exactly 100 radians per second for this series circuit bandwidth.
A higher quality factor compresses the half power frequencies closer together, sharpening the response peak.
